name: Nanyuki Town
tagline: The working centre on the equator
description: The main street and market area, with the shops, the banks, the supermarkets and the equator marker that every visitor stops at. It is a functional Kenyan town serving the farms and conservancies around it, and it is where daily business gets done.
bestFor: Anyone without a vehicle or needing services daily
pros: Banks, supermarkets and services all here
Matatus and boda bodas for local transport
cons: Dusty and busy through the day
Mount Kenya views blocked in the centre

name: Nanyuki West and the Ol Pejeta Road
tagline: Out towards the conservancy, with the space
description: The area running west of town along the road to Ol Pejeta Conservancy, with farms, cottages and lodges spread across open country. It is where much of the resident expatriate and conservation community lives, in houses with land and Mount Kenya behind them.
bestFor: Longer stays with a vehicle wanting a house and a garden
pros: Close to Ol Pejeta and the conservancies
Where the resident community actually lives
cons: Power cuts and water supply vary by property

name: Mount Kenya Wildlife Estate and Sweetwaters
tagline: Gated properties with game on the doorstep
description: The estates and lodges just outside town where private houses sit inside conservancy fences with zebra and giraffe moving through the grounds. It is the most comfortable and by far the most expensive way to be based here, and the internet is the best in the district.
bestFor: Anyone with the budget who wants wildlife outside the window
pros: Game visible from the property itself
Best power and internet reliability locally
Security and services handled by the estate
cons: A vehicle is required for everything

name: Timau
tagline: The farming belt on the northern slopes
description: A small settlement about twenty-five minutes northeast on the road to Isiolo, in the wheat and flower farming country on Mount Kenya's northern slopes. It is higher, cooler and greener than Nanyuki, and it is where much of the region's agriculture is based.
bestFor: Anyone connected to farming or wanting cooler, greener country
cons: Twenty-five minutes from the town's services

name: Naro Moru
tagline: The trailhead village south of town
description: A small village half an hour south, best known as the start of the Naro Moru route up Mount Kenya, with a river lodge and a handful of guesthouses serving climbers. It is cheaper than Nanyuki and closer to the mountain gate.
bestFor: Climbers and anyone using the mountain regularly
pros: Closest base for the Naro Moru route
cons: Half an hour from Nanyuki's services
